Unknown: current implied yields, basis, and roll after the FOMC, because AU rates were not refreshed to the FX date.
Horizon is weeks, not a patient positive-carry hold; if housing data stall, carry becomes the reason to exit.

expression_comparison.chosen_because: The discrepancy lives in AUD still printing as a mid-to-high-percentile research level against USD after hard AU housing damage, while AU and US yields are already 97th–99th percentile. Long duration fights sticky inflation; the US bull steepener needs a US growth break that gauges do not show; AU-US rates RV is date-mismatched and can fail if the RBA cannot cut. Vol is not unusually compelling versus this spot. Short AUDUSD is the cleaner defensive expression of policy-driven slowdown plus risk-off.

considered_rates.assessment: Verified: US 10Y 4.94 on 2026-09-17 is 1y 97.8th percentile (+45bp 3m, -7bp on the day after the hike); AU 2Y 4.835 on 2026-09-09 is 1y 99.8th percentile. A pure growth-scare would own long duration. Rejected as the primary expression because US CPI/PPI/import prices and AU inflation 82 keep a policy-error/inflation tail live, AU yields are eight days stale and pre-FOMC, and 99th-percentile yields have already marked a lot of tightness. Stagflation is toxic for bonds and compatible with short AUD.

State versus change: US activity/labor remain hot (69/75); the new information is AU housing hard data and a hike that futures had already assigned >90% odds.

Normalization: AU inflation 82 versus activity 54 / labor 50 / consumer 48 is restriction-plus-slowdown, not a clean easing cycle. NZ is weaker on growth gauges but already cheaper in NZDUSD (1y 21st / 5y 11th).
Historical reference: AUDUSD is not the extreme (1y 75th); the extremes are AUDNZD/AUDCAD and the yield percentiles. Mean reversion of AUDNZD is a yardstick, not the trade.
Market-implied assumption: a delivered hike plus 99th-percentile AU yields should already have done the AUD damage if FX were mechanically following rates; it has not.

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if official AU housing/transaction data stabilize or reverse while Fed/RBA communication closes further tightening, or if AUDUSD outperforms on a sustained risk-on/commodity impulse that the housing channel cannot explain. Right-thesis/wrong-timing if housing keeps deteriorating but AUD is bid solely on carry versus still-higher AU 2Y yields.
trade.mispricing: Market pricing already embeds a delivered, >90%-odds Fed hike and near-record AU bond yields, but AUDUSD remains a mid-to-high-percentile research print rather than a stress print. The gap is AU growth/credit damage versus still-firm AUD, not an unpriced US hike. AUDNZD at the 5y 99.96th percentile is the statistical extreme, but that cross is the wrong object: NZ labor/consumer gauges are weaker than AU, NZ rates are unavailable, and an AUD/NZD pair does not own risk-off.

trade.thesis: The causal mechanism is late-cycle policy error: the RBA tightening channel is already breaking Australian housing (NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% YoY, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% off peak) while AU inflation remains the hottest retained gauge (82). The Fed has just delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% into still-hot US inflation/labor, so policy cannot easily offset the growth hit. That combination is stagflationary for duration and defensive for high-beta FX. AUDUSD still sits only around the 1y 75th / 5y 84th percentile on the 2026-09-17 ECB reference snapshot, so FX has not fully marked the housing/growth discrepancy that AU yields (99th percentile as of 2026-09-09) have already spent.
why_now: AU housing hard data and the realized Sep 16 FOMC hike are contemporaneous, not sequential.
AUDUSD is already changing on the margin (ECB-reference -0.99% over 5d, -0.26% on 2026-09-17) while remaining only a 1y 74.8th-percentile level, so the move is starting without being spent.
Post-hike UST 2Y/10Y each fell 7bp on 2026-09-17, showing the priced hike is not a clean hawkish follow-through in duration; FX can still mark the AU-US growth split.
The Saudi Oman workaround modestly reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, weakening a commodity offset that would otherwise bid AUD.

Evidence that AUDNZD's 5y extreme is the actual mispricing and that NZ's weaker labor/consumer gauges dominate AU housing.
